Subject: Re: Serving mode evaluation — next steps & info needed

Samir,

Thanks again for the 30-minute sync today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can model economics and propose a pilot: 

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Primary priority: low latency for chat experiences in the US, SLA expectation ~100ms median for short prompts.
- Traffic shape: mostly daytime spikes (09:00–18:00 PT), occasional batch export jobs overnight.
- Data residency: US-only for now.
- Security: SOC 2 and customer-managed KMS are required for production.

Key decision axes we discussed (so you have the framing we used):
- Hosted API: fastest to production, pay-as-you-go (per-token) — good if usage is spiky and you want no infra ops.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and lower unit $ at scale (reserved commit + burst).
- Private VPC / on-prem: best for strict network controls and full isolation; longer onboarding and separate procurement.

Asks for pricing model accuracy (please reply with any of these by EOD Monday):
1) Expected average QPS and peak concurrent requests (sample numbers for business/peak day)
2) Avg tokens per request (in/out) and expected tokens/month
3) Any hard constraints on SLA/uptime or audit windows
4) Procurement timeline and target go-live (month/quarter)

I attached a simple template you can drop numbers into (acme_traffic_forecast_q2.csv) — that will let us produce a quick per-mode cost comparison.

Proposed immediate next step: once we have forecast numbers, we’ll send a one-page cost comparison (hosted vs dedicated vs private) and a recommended pilot configuration (30–90 day) tailored to your traffic shape.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin

Chloe — thanks for the clear recap. Filling out the numbers below and attaching our forecast.

Answers to your asks (high level):
1) Expected QPS: avg ~12 QPS; peak ~95 QPS (10–15 minute spikes during launches).
2) Avg tokens: request payload ~80 tokens, response ~220 tokens => avg ~300 tokens per interaction. Estimated tokens/month: ~550M tokens.
3) SLA: we need ~99.9% uptime for production and PII is allowable if stored encrypted at rest (customer-managed KMS preferred).
4) Timeline: procurement target is end of May; pilot ideally in June. Budget target for initial pilot is ~ $60k/mo OPEX.

Notes: We prefer dedicated instances if the unit economics make sense since long-term we expect steady growth. However, if the delta between hosted and dedicated is small for pilot volume, a hosted pilot with strong telemetry is acceptable.

Attaching the forecast CSV with hourly estimates.

Subject: Re: Serving mode evaluation — cost options & recommended pilot

Samir — great, thanks for the numbers and the CSV. I ran a first-pass model (attached) and below is a succinct summary to align on expectations. I kept assumptions conservative on tokens and a small margin for overhead.

Quick cost summary (monthly, estimates):
- Hosted API (pay-as-you-go): ~ $74k / month — includes per-token billing blended for generation + embedding calls, with no infra commitments. Best if you want to avoid procurement and iterate quickly.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): ~ $48k / month with a 6-month reserved commit at pilot scale (assumes a modest share of a GPU pool with autoscale burst). Lower unit cost but requires a contract for reserved capacity.
- Private VPC (managed deployment): ~ $95k / month + one-time setup ~ $35k — higher ops and infra overhead but meets strict network isolation; 4–6 week onboarding.

Notes on the numbers:
- Hosted assumes typical batching and Redwood’s caching heuristics; we can reduce ~10–20% at runtime with more aggressive prefix caching.
- Dedicated savings come from reserved GPU amortization; we modeled your peak shapes and included buffer headroom for bursts.
- Private VPC includes a managed-control-plane fee and estimated egress/network costs for US regions.

Recommended pilot approach given your constraints:
1) 60–90 day Dedicated pilot with a modest 20% reserved commit to capture unit-cost benefits while keeping flexibility. We can scope the commit to match pilot medians and allow autoscale for launch spikes.
2) Parallel telemetry on Hosted API for feature experimentation to avoid blocking product iterations.
3) If procurement timelines push, we can start with Hosted for first 2–3 weeks (fast onboarding) and convert committed Dedicated mid-pilot — we’ll credit the hosted spend toward the commit.

Next steps we suggest (can do this week):
- You confirm the forecast numbers in the CSV (we’ll adjust the model).
- We provide a 1-page deal sketch (commit sizes, expected monthly charge, SLA language) for procurement.
- SE kickoff (Rishi) to map integration work and SSO/KMS flow.

I attached the detailed cost workbook (redwood_cost_model_acme.xlsx) — it includes sensitivity runs if your tokens/month moves +/- 25%.

If this looks directionally right, I’ll put together the deal sketch and a pilot SOW draft.

Best,

Subject: Re: Serving mode evaluation — technical notes on pilot options

Samir / Chloe — quick technical addendum to Chloe’s cost notes that will affect the pilot SOW and timeline:

- Integration & onboarding: for Dedicated we typically provision the reserve and can be ready for a limited pilot in ~2–3 weeks (assuming signed SOW and access to VPC peering info). Private VPC adds 3–6 weeks primarily for network config and KMS integration.
- Performance levers: with your token shapes, enabling continuous batching and KV prefix caching gives the best price/latency tradeoff; we’ll instrument perf metrics (p95/p99, token rate) and tune batch windows dynamically.
- Security: we’ll need KMS key setup and an SCIM/SSO integration for seat provisioning in the pilot. If procurement requires a BAA or additional contracts, factor that into the timeline.
- Monitoring: we’ll pipe token-level and route-level metrics into your Splunk/Datadog (or our Console) during pilot for clear cost attribution.

Happy to run a 30-minute SE session to walk through the integration checklist and map the 3-week plan for Dedicated pilot.

-Rishi
